subject: Urgent: DPA redline — data-minimization & telemetry exhibit needed
messages:
From: David Foster <david.foster@medtech.co>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medtech.co; procurement@medtech.co
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline — telemetry retention & data minimization exhibit

Karthik —

Thanks for the fast demo last week. Our legal team attached a clean DPA redline (v3) and a short list of changes we need for procurement to move forward. High-level asks:

- Telemetry retention: all inference telemetry and usage traces must be purged within 24 hours unless explicitly included in a signed exhibit.
- Embeddings and derived features: prohibit using customer embeddings for analytics, model training, or downstream profiling.
- Subprocessor transparency: provide an exhaustive list of subprocessors and SOC2 evidence for those handling transient runtime artifacts.
- KV cache / runtime snapshots: any runtime cache that could contain customer inputs must be non-persistent and deleted after 24 hours.

We attached the proposed redline (MedTech_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Can your team confirm you can accept these or propose a narrow exhibit that limits our exposure? Procurement is targeting sign-off by next week.

Appreciate a short call if helpful.

-David

--
David Foster
Director, IT Procurement
MedTech Solutions
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline — telemetry retention & data minimization exhibit

Forwarding MedTech's redlines — they pushed hard on data-minimization (24h) and a strict ban on embeddings usage for analytics. Procurement wants sign-off next week.

Quick product/security read:
- Feasibility notes (product):
  * 24-hour absolute purge for telemetry is feasible for hosted endpoints by default, but we need to define what counts as "telemetry" vs "operational logs" (error traces, end-to-end traces, billing tokens). Batching/k-v cache metadata may be accidentally classified as telemetry.
  * Embedding prohibition for analytics is tricky: we generate embeddings for customer features (search, personalization). We can offer a carveout where embeddings used for product features are kept ephemeral or scoped to customer-owned projects, but we need to preserve some aggregated metrics for quality monitoring.
  * KV cache: we can enforce ephemeral (in-memory) cache with TTL < 24h; for Dedicated/Private deployments this varies and may need contractual language limiting retention only for hosted mode.

- Product ask: need a short exhibit (one page) that enumerates allowable telemetry types, retention windows, and acceptable analytics (aggregated/anonymized). I propose a default 90-day aggregated telemetry window for product-quality metrics and a 24-hour raw telemetry purge for request traces unless customer opts-in to a longer retention with explicit exhibit.

- Requested from Security (Olga): what evidence can we share now (SOC2 summary, subprocessor list)? Also: is an encrypted/staging-only KV cache feasible?

Next steps: Olga/laura — can you confirm acceptable mitigation options and whether Legal will accept a 90-day aggregated telemetry compromise + a Data Minimization Exhibit that narrows embeddings use? I'll draft the exhibit if we have alignment.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline — telemetry retention & data minimization exhibit

Team —

We should treat this as a security gating item for the deal. Initial security stance:

- Subprocessors: we can provide an exhaustive list for hosted services (AWS, WasmCacheInc, VectorStoreCo) and a SOC2 summary for those vendors. We cannot share full third-party contracts but can produce evidence (attestations).
- Telemetry classification: request traces and error logs that contain user input must be redacted and eligible for 24h purge. Operational metrics (cpu/gpu utilization, request counts, token counts) are less sensitive and can be aggregated.
- Embeddings: we cannot accept a blanket prohibition on using embeddings for quality/ops analytics because that materially impairs our monitoring and anomaly detection. Proposal: allow embeddings for internal quality/ops if they are run through a one-way hash/aggregation pipeline and only ever used in aggregate; explicitly forbid training on customer embeddings unless customer signs a separate training consent.
- KV cache: feasible to enforce ephemeral-by-default for hosted; for Dedicated we need contractual language requiring customer opt-in for any persistent cache.

Action items for me:
1) Prepare a one-page Data Minimization Exhibit that codifies definitions ("telemetry", "operational metrics", "derived features") and retention windows (24h raw traces; 90d aggregated metrics).
2) Share subprocessor list + SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and a suggested non-disclosing list format.
3) Provide technical notes for Product on how embeddings can be anonymized/hashed and what guarantees we can give.

Timeline: I can have the exhibit draft and vendor attestation bundle by EOD tomorrow. Legal (Laura) — will that be fast enough to keep procurement on their timeline?

- Olga
Senior Information Security Manager
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: David Foster <david.foster@medtech.co>, legal@medtech.co
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — telemetry retention & data minimization exhibit

David / MedTech team —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. We want to get you to signature while protecting both parties. Proposed compromise below (we'll put this in a short Data Minimization Exhibit to attach to the DPA):

- Definitions: we will define "raw telemetry/request traces" as any logged request or stack trace containing customer-provided content; "operational metrics" as aggregated system metrics (counts, latencies, error rates, token usage).
- Retention: raw telemetry/request traces — automatic purge within 24 hours by default for hosted customers; customers can request extended retention only via an explicit exhibit and opting into a higher support tier. Operational metrics — retained up to 90 days, aggregated at tenant-level and not associated with PII.
- Embeddings: embeddings will not be used for model training or profiling of individual users. We will allow embeddings to be used for operational quality/aggregation if they are deterministically hashed and only processed in aggregate. We will not use customer embeddings to train models without explicit, signed consent.
- KV cache/runtime snapshots: hosted runtime caches will be ephemeral and configured with a maximum TTL of 24 hours. For Dedicated/Private deployments, persistence is configurable but must be contractually scoped; Redwood will document configuration options in the exhibit.
- Subprocessors & evidence: we will provide a complete subprocessor list for hosted services and an SOC2 summary for subprocessors handling runtime artifacts. We will provide an attestation package within 48 hours.

If this aligns, we'll produce the one-page exhibit and redline the DPA accordingly. Olga and Laura will attach the SOC2 summary and the subprocessor list to the exhibit. If MedTech needs a shorter retention window for aggregated metrics we can discuss but it will have product tradeoffs (reduced monitoring and slower incident response).

Next step: proposed 30-minute call Monday to walk through the exhibit and show the technical controls (KV cache TTL, hashing pipeline for embeddings). Otherwise we'll send the exhibit + attachments and a DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
